title: Mitigate tokens/sec oscillation during in-place model snapshot upgrades (hosted/dedicated/private)
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Over the past 48 hours we've seen recurring oscillations in tokens/sec and first-token latency across mixed-variant serving pools during in-place model snapshot upgrades. The pattern shows short periods (30-120s) of degraded throughput followed by overshoot recovery. Affected environments include Hosted (multitenant), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC nodes running the snapshot rollout logic.

Hypothesis: The snapshot upgrade path triggers a transient rebalancing of model shards and KV cache priming. In-flight requests see repeated cache misses and kernel re-selection churn, producing lower sustained tokens/sec and sporadic TTFT regressions. Traffic shaping/backpressure is amplifying the oscillation because warmup signals are being treated like capacity signals (aggressive shedder ramp-down then sudden ramp-up).

Why urgent: Several enterprise customers escalated with production regressions for long-running chat sessions (notable on 512/1024 token contexts) and reported increased error rates on dedicated pools. This has SLA implications and is causing on-call paging.
steps_to_reproduce: Run a snapshot model rollout on a dedicated pool with mixed small/big context workloads (sample script: infra/test-rollout.sh).
Simulate steady open-chat traffic at normal qps with multiplexing on MUX router. Use longer sessions (avg 600 tokens).
Trigger in-place snapshot upgrade (no drain) and observe tokens/sec and first-token latency for 10 minutes around the rollout window.
Expected: small transient warmup with modest latency bump. Observed: 30-120s oscillating troughs in tokens/sec with 2-3x TTFT spike and partial request backpressure leading to retries.
telemetry: Primary dashboards: Console > Model Pools > Pool-aggregates (tokens/sec, TTFT P50/P95/P99), Router > Queue Depth, KV cache hit ratio by model shard.
Alert rules fired: tokens-per-second-drop (>30% sustained) and TTFT spike (>2x baseline) across 3 regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-sg).
Repro logs: kernel-selector churn traces show back-to-back kernel selection events for same request id in 12% of sampled flows during upgrade window.
Customer traces: Request IDs from corp-acct-241 show repeated retry loops with 'prefetch-miss' tags aligned with upgrade TTLs.
mitigation_actions_taken: Immediate: Enabled soft drain on snapshot rollout controller to allow inflight-request completion before switching active weight (reduced churning).
Deployed a temporary smoothing policy in the router: soft-rate-limit with 15s linear ramp instead of instantaneous capacity shift for active variants.
Disabled aggressive KV prefetch eviction for the duration of the rollout to stabilize cache hit ratios on affected shards.
Notified customers via status page and opened support bridges for the three impacted tenants.
short_term_plan: Ship hotfix to the rollout controller to perform graceful in-flight migration: wait-for-inflight + staggered weight shift across shards.
Introduce a roll-forward config flag `smoothing.window_ms` default 15000 for hosted and dedicated that can be tightened later.
Add a guard in router to treat warmup traffic as 'warming' not 'capacity' for shedder decisions (avoid immediate ramp-down).
Monitor for 24h post-deploy; if oscillation persists, deploy secondary KV-level pinning for hot shards.
long_term_work: Design: formalize upgrade choreography that ties KV cache priming to rollout phases with metrics-based progression (traffic-weight thresholds + cache-hit prerequisites).
Infra: add rollout canary traffic routing where a small percentage of sessions are mirrored to new snapshot to validate cache behavior before cutover.
Runtime: implement kernel-selection debounce to avoid reselecting kernels for a request more than once in 5s unless explicit failure occurs.
Observability: add dedicated 'upgrade impact' view that correlates rollout events with cache and kernel churn metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens/sec troughs around upgrades reduced to <10% below baseline for >95% of affected pools during 30m windows.
TTFT P95 uplift limited to <1.5x baseline during rollouts on canary and one production pool, verified across regions.
No new errors introduced and SLO error budget burn from rollout incidents < 5% for the week following fix.
Automated e2e test that simulates snapshot rollout + mixed-session traffic passes in CI with deterministic assertions on tokens/sec and TTFT.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Deploy controller hotfix to a single non-critical hosted pool and a dedicated internal test pool. Run 6 hour smoke with synthetic traffic (12:00-18:00 UTC).
Stage 2 (pilot customers): Enable smoothing.window_ms=15000 for 3 enterprise customers historically affected; coordinate support windows. Monitor and gather traces.
Stage 3 (region expand): Ramp to all hosted pools in us-west1 and eu-west1 with 2h observation windows per expansion step.
Stage 4 (global): Flip default for dedicated/private rollout controller and add rollout safety toggle in Console (off by default until verified).
rollback_criteria: If tokens/sec drop exceeds 25% for >10 minutes in any canary pool, rollback to previous rollout-controller image.
If TTFT P95 exceeds 2x baseline or error rates spike >0.5% absolute, roll back the smoothing change and investigate logs.
Automated rollback invoked if kernel-selector churn metric increases beyond established baseline by 30%.
